boundary_rationale: The lamed and mem triplets (3:34-36, 3:37-39) turn from the compassion statement to a theodicy reflection posing rhetorical questions about justice and divine sovereignty, continuing the same third-person wisdom-style register with no first-person geber speech across the six verses. Lines opening with an interrogative particle inside the mem triplet stand in exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.37, Lam.3.39): the first spliced at byte tier as מִ֣י זֶ֤ה אָמַר֙ וַתֶּ֔הִי אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א צִוָּֽה (oshb:Lam.3.37, byte tier; WEB “Who is he who says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord doesn’t command it?”, web:Lam.3.37), the second opening on מַה (oshb:Lam.3.39, byte tier) and closing the triplet as “Why should a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” (web:Lam.3.39); the intervening verse opens מִפִּ֤י (oshb:Lam.3.38, byte tier) with no interrogative particle in the source, though its own WEB rendering poses a question. This closing question is one candidate hinge into the cohortative confession that opens the next triplet, though whether the turn belongs with the reflection ending here or the confession beginning next is held rather than decided. Lam.3.39 is itself a marked ketiv/qere verse, carrying one note rather than a doubled note; the spliced particle stands at the verse's own opening, not at the variant, which falls on the verse's final word.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this span through the nun triplet (Lam.3.40-Lam.3.42) was considered because the closing rhetorical question at Lam.3.39 anticipates the confession that follows, so the third-person reflection could be read as continuing thematically up to the cohortative onset itself; it was rejected because the shift from third-person reflection to first-person-plural cohortative confession at Lam.3.40 is a clearer voice-based seam than treating the rhetorical-question close of Lam.3.39 as the boundary by itself.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A ketiv/qere note sits at Lam.3.39, on the mem triplet's own closing verse, disclosed by its count; no Hebrew splice in this span reaches the variant word, though the quoted WEB rendering of that verse follows the qere plural reading rather than the ketiv. The lamed and mem triplets close on SAMEKH marks at Lam.3.36 and Lam.3.39, continuing from the kaf triplet's own SAMEKH mark at Lam.3.33 one verse behind this span's onset (single-witness corroboration, tier-3 weak under the Writings addendum). Labeling this span hope_meditation rather than a bespoke theodicy category is a one-sentence operative-category deviation this span discloses: its content argues justice and sovereignty in the third person rather than continuing the first-person wait-and-hope posture of the triplets just before it, kept here under the same closed vocabulary as the surrounding material.
